paper.title: RNA-Seq Based Transcriptome Analysis of Aspergillus oryzae DSM 1863 Grown on Glucose, Acetate and an Aqueous Condensate from the Fast Pyrolysis of Wheat Straw
paper.authors: Kubisch C, Kovilein A, Aliyu H, Ochsenreither K.
paper.association_evidence: Data Availability Statement: 'The RNA-seq data underlying this study were uploaded to the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) database under the following BioProject ID: PRJNA845824.'

study_summary.objective: Describe how A. oryzae DSM 1863 responds transcriptionally to growth on 20% detoxified pyrolytic aqueous condensate (PAC) from wheat straw compared with pure acetate and glucose.
study_summary.experimental_design: Shake-flask cultures in a defined mineral medium at 30 C with glucose, acetate or 20% detoxified PAC as carbon source, harvested at 24 h (glucose, acetate) or 48 h (PAC) to match growth phase; 3 biological replicates each.
study_summary.main_finding: About 3,460 genes were differentially expressed; acetate and PAC cultures looked alike (ribosome and RNA-processing genes up, transmembrane transport down), and only pyruvate metabolism differed significantly between them.

dsm1863_mineral_flask.note: mineral salts medium with ammonium sulfate
500 mL flasks with 100 mL medium, 100 rpm

glucose_reference.note: glucose is the reference carbon source against which acetate and PAC are compared

carbon-source shift relative to the glucose reference

notes: Which run is glucose, acetate or PAC comes from the SRA experiment titles / library names; the BioSample attributes only list 'sample 1-9' and the replicate number.
Glucose and acetate were sampled at 24 h and PAC at 48 h to match growth phase, so substrate and time are confounded by design.
